# About Vanessa Kenniche Sanocka {#about}

::: {.lead}
Machine learning and data science engineer
:::

Engineering degree from the [CMI](https://reseau-figure.fr/les-cursus-master-en-ingenierie) program at Paris Nanterre University.

Specialized in quantitative economics and public policy analysis, complemented by data and machine learning engineering expertise forged in direct contact with audit teams and data scientists. Expertise in end-to-end project leadership: econometric modeling, large-scale and sensitive data processing, design and industrialization of data and AI pipelines (RAG, ETL, MLOps, containerized deployment in sovereign environments), transforming complex analyses into accessible recommendations for stakeholders. International experience and ability to present to diverse audiences, from magistrates to technical teams. Structured approach focused on reproducibility, knowledge transfer and decision impact, supported by a hybrid data scientist and engineer profile that anchors tool design in real business needs.

# Professional Experience {#experience}

## French Court of Audit | Since 2023

### Machine Learning & Data Engineer {#experience-ml}

::: {.role-context}
Current position within the Digital and Data Department. Mission: equip the Court with production-grade data and AI tools (semantic search engines, legacy ETL rewrites, LLM agents, analytical platforms) to support the work of audit teams, magistrates and data scientists. Hybrid profile combining the domain experience gained on the audit and data-science side with the end-to-end engineering expertise required to ship in sovereign and air-gapped environments.
:::

#### PRISME : semantic search engine over the public corpus of the French Court of Audit, available to audit teams, magistrates and domain experts

End-to-end RAG pipeline over ~35,000 Court publications (~2M indexed paragraphs), from table-of-contents extraction to natural-language sourced answer generation. Fourteen-stage modular chain: two-pass semantic *chunking* combining LLM-based TOC extraction and *fuzzy split* via TOC-zone fingerprint (original idea designed to bypass the classic indexing pitfalls of long PDFs), *breadcrumb* contextual enrichment inspired by Anthropic's Contextual Retrieval, dual indexing in Elasticsearch (textual BM25 + vectorial KNN HNSW over Qwen3-8B embeddings), hybrid retrieval via RRF, MMR diversification, cross-encoder Qwen3 *reranking*, Mistral generation gated by a refusal threshold calibrated against hallucinations. Evaluation through manual *gold standard* and RAGAS, *ablation testing* at every stage. Next.js / FastAPI interface, multi-service Docker deployment in a sovereign air-gapped environment (Nexus registry, multi-target *justfile*, dual-VM SSH, offline *builds*, *feature flags* in production). Scientific paper in conference format (ACL/IEEE) under writing on the methodological contributions.

#### ANAPAYE : rewrite of the public-sector payroll analysis tool used by the regional and territorial chambers for their audits

Migration of a legacy Talend ETL pipeline to a modern Python chain for processing payroll files in the XHL / Hélios / PES v2 formats. Modular architecture separating application, pipeline and data layer, with *streaming* XML parsing for memory efficiency and Pydantic validation. Multi-schema PostgreSQL storage driven by SQLModel and explicitly managed Alembic migrations. Multi-page Streamlit application for the audit teams, with embedded Apache Superset dashboards via SDK and dynamic RLS clauses. Supervised *machine learning* module for anomaly detection on imbalanced HR data, currently being industrialized under MLflow. Multi-service Docker containerization, internal Nexus registry and *justfile* orchestration for air-gapped deployment, with advanced asyncio on heavy pipelines (semaphores, *retry / backoff*, *checkpoint* resume).

#### Wikam : knowledge graph exposed to an AI agent via Model Context Protocol, alternative to classical RAG for the Court's structured institutional memory

Design of an MCP server wrapping the internal wiki to let an LLM agent navigate the institution's procedural memory (audit organization, investigation flow, magistrate / verifier / counter-rapporteur roles) instead of receiving the raw markdown. The model accesses tools for title search, page retrieval, hierarchical traversal and neighborhood lookup, and invokes them on demand. The approach is relevant when the content is already well-chaptered and where classical RAG chunking would introduce noise. Sequenced adoption strategy: NetworkX graph as a POC, plugging in PRISME's embeddings infrastructure for hybrid RAG, full-entity-extraction GraphRAG envisaged only as a last resort.

#### Structuring ten years of Court of Audit recommendations into a queryable database : about 75,000 recommendations extracted from 35,600 reports (2015-2025)

Asynchronous LLM pipeline for identifying and structuring the "recommendations" sections of reports, never extracted systematically before. Direct LLM detection on the first or last characters of the document depending on the typical placement of recommendations, preceded by a heuristic *scoring* phase (numbering regex, suspicious gap detection, second-chance mechanism). Asynchronous Mistral pipeline with *exponential backoff*, pause on error streaks, JSONL *checkpoint* resume. Dedicated Elasticsearch indexing with *nested mapping* to preserve metadata, embeddings and original recipient, CSV / XLSX exports for the audit teams.
